title: One-slot profitable-incumbent fresh-signal rotation
thesis: In the fixed 30 USDT one-slot DRA lane, when a fresh confirmed DRA signal arrives while the incumbent lot already satisfies the existing +1% estimated-net next-open safety floor, conditionally selling that incumbent and replacing it with the fresh signal will reduce blocked opportunity cost and improve fee-adjusted total PnL without increasing capital or drawdown.
mechanism: The one-slot parent repeatedly blocks fresh DRA signals while profitable-but-subtarget inventory occupies the only slot. The candidate reserves the fresh signal only when the incumbent is already at the existing +1% net floor, attempts the incumbent sale first at the next hourly open under the unchanged +1% realized-net floor, buys the replacement at that same open only after a successful sale, and otherwise cancels the replacement without adding exposure.
economic_rationale: The frozen one-slot baseline is near fully utilized and recorded 273 blocked Design confirmations and 117 blocked Validation confirmations. Event-driven rotation tests whether some of that opportunity cost comes from retaining already-profitable inventory rather than from genuinely underwater capital, while preserving the 30 USDT cap, profit-only boundary, fees, adverse slippage, and next-open execution.
